exposure: Placental position (anterior, posterior, fundal, lateral, low-lying)
cohort: The study included 270 singleton pregnancies between 14-40 weeks gestation.
finding: Lateral placentation showed significantly higher rates of complications, including antepartum hemorrhage, IUGR, emergency cesarean sections, and NICU admission rates.
mod_finding: Posterior and fundal placentas were associated with higher rates of normal vaginal delivery, while lateral placentation had higher rates of emergency cesarean sections.
